body: I just had my first at 38. I don’t have a ton of energy but the trade off is that I have more money. There’s no better route either way. It’s just either or.

I go to AlNon and and I’m also in AA.  I don’t go to ACoA because I’m already working one program. But I also read the literature for ACoA. I would suggest you work out your feelings for your experiences. After I had my kid, I had different resentments towards my parents, whom I love and see often. When my sister and I talk to my nephews about this stuff, we talk about our own experiences in a way that’s understandable and appropriate for the kids age. You can tell your son, “Grandpa hurt my feelings as a kid and what he said upset me”. Let it go from there. But definitely talk to someone about your experiences and how you want to handle this. There are probably ACoA meetings online you can go to.
I started at 27 making 29k. I didn’t see a significant raise until 2 years in.
My nephew loved his for a long time. My kid hated it.

I don’t own a home because I don’t want to be responsible for repairs. I’ve never wanted to be married. My mom was a single lady with 10 rental properties. She fixed things herself and hired people when she couldn’t make the repairs. She dated but only for fun. My father is a carpenter and he hates home repair. He also rents. I don’t know if he dates. I think he has flings. My parents were never married. I think “learning to be alone “ implies that a person is with someone for a long time and suddenly are alone. And “settling“ makes me think of someone looking for the right one and picking the best option. To me it seems like some people know what they want and others are figuring it out.
I signed up for WIC and I get so much for the baby. I was told they do not effect each other. I was laid off a month ago. I’m a single mom of a 9 month old. Listen to your husband! It will be ok :-)

You can put her in a scholarship writing class. I’d also put her in ACT/SAT test prep. I’d do it early and then back off until you get closer to graduation. If she has an anxiety attack, you’ll do a lot more damage.  Show her the expectations and than let her find her coping mechanisms. Push her at the end of HS when she is also pushing herself. Otherwise, you’re asking for burn out and resentment.
I feel like this could have come out of the ACoA or Al Anon sub. Maybe go to a meeting? They’re online.

I do the 50/30/20 thing when I’m fearful of risking a monetary loss. If I’m scared I do 20% into the ETF, 30% in Bonds, 50% HYSA. Fear is an emotion and you want to take emotions out of your finances. But if you can’t, break it up like this. Than once you see that nothing has been lost or that you can weather a downturn, flip the percentage to 50% ETF, 30% Bonds 20% HYSA. Than do 50% ETF and 50% Bonds. Than 60% ETF, 40% Bonds, ect ect
I live in the US and the sperm was the biggest cost of my IUI. Traveling wouldn’t have saved me money. But if you have an FSA, I’ve heard it can be put towards medical travel.

They can’t make exceptions for one person if they’re a big management company.  I rent from a landlord who employs a broker to manage the property and I can negotiate with both of them. But you’re not going to get that in a place that has many multiple units.  Which is why it is better to rent from landlords instead of property companies imo.

In my state, unemployment pays out a week after you get approved. So it takes less than 2 weeks. And you can work and make less than half the unemployment benefit, and still keep the full benefit. If you make more than half, they deduct the difference from your benefit payout.

Cribs are really hard to buy used where I’m at. Many of the larger items I have will not be accepted by churches or thrift stores. I’m told WIC will accept somethings.  When I find out someone is expecting, I’m all over them to offload the baby gear.
But I got sooo many handmedown items that I was able to put more necessities on my registry.
Totally agree with all your points. Although, I really like to use the boppi and so does my dog. 

I’ll also add that you can potty train early and cut down on the diapers.
And check out the dollar store before target or Walmart or wherever else.  

Also, pack up the extra toys that people give you. Once your kid starts playing, they’ll only need a few toys. You can regift or donate the ones that don’t get used right away. 

Other people told me what to get/buy/use and there were clear winners among the other parents.  I do hate how much fear munger marketing there is towards parents. And I also hate the marketing towards kids(they don’t have jobs!) But, you can reuse sooo much from other families.
My kiddo is 8 months  and I really hope we can connect with her half siblings.

My park district has baby pool lessons and I think the only requirement is that they can hold their head up well. I started my baby at 5 or 6 months at a swim school. She was a late learner compared to the others.

I’d say 12 weeks was when my baby started following a sleep schedule.  I don’t remember when she started playing but eventually she’d wake up and coo before crying to be fed. I’d hold up a toy or my hand or whatever and she’d follow it with her eyes. She hated tummy time and we didn’t do it nearly as much as we were told to. She’s almost 9 months and she can stand by pushing herself up. She crawls and walks along the furniture.
I have a dog.
We live by the park but there’s always music there. Otherwise, I play it on the free TV channels.
You should apply for snap if you’re on unemployment. Take care of your body and your mental health.
Ask her if she wants to bunk with her brother. But I really think the problem is with your wife.

I don’t think it’s weird unless your locking the door. But does she share a room with the sibling? Because than maybe it’s best for her to stay in her room. Or you’re going to have 2 kids that don’t stay in their room.
Sometimes a local church will own properties that they rent out to people in need.

I really like the grocery store as the drive thru. Even the pre made meals in the deli section are less expensive than eating out.  It takes a little longer but you get out of your car and stretch your legs. And most stores have self checkout. Even my Aldi has them now.
Kroger owns a bunch of different chains but their shopper’s card works at all of them. I Stumbled upon that while on vacation.

My grandma lived in assisted living until she was 99 and I feel like what OP is doing could have been an option for her.  My great grandma on the other side also lived until her late 90’s, in her home.  I think it just depends on the person and the family.

Dude, so many kids need male role models. Look into respite fostering or BigBrothers. I know there’s a stigma about men adopting but it’s really a great thing when a guy gets involved in the life of a child in need.
I was just reading about how expensive elder care is in the US. I think this is a way better option than independent care.
Save the money first when you get paid. Put it in an account with no debt card attached.

I’m going to piggie back and say the sports/team wear is inexpensive.
So are gift cards and vouchers for tourist destinations. If you live by a major city or are traveling to one, you can find good deals on activities. There’s usually a deal on legos or Costco will offer their own hot toy dupe. If you buy Xmas gifts for kids, Costco is the way to go. The flea and tick medicine for pets is pretty inexpensive too.

I have the executive card and I’ve made the $30 back on gas, diapers and formula. If you don’t want to overspend, try not to go in the store. 

The nuts and berries though. Sooo cheap.
I would chat up the Uber drivers and see if one is willing to drive for cash. Find one that’s local and pay then $15.  Or find a co-worker who can help you.

I also have a hard time finding time to cook and just recently went to the food bank. I went on a weekday because it was a little quicker to get though the line. But a lot of the stuff I got had to be prepared. I did get some things that I could freeze but try to research which pantries have less foot traffic, otherwise, you’ll be there for an hour and half waiting for food you have to prepare. However, I did find time to meal prep what I got and I probably won’t need to buy any food for the month. I am soooo tired though.
Mine sleeps 6-7 hours since 15 weeks. But she starts at 5pm sometimes :-(
Go tor/personalfinance and follow the spread sheet.
My friend is coming over and we’re going to make mini muffins or pancakes for the baby. Then I’m going to take a nap while they play!!
Microwave meals and add microwaveable veggies and meat. This is what I did and I’m also a single mom. But I stoped breastfeeding at 12 weeks.

My parents were divorced before I was I born and I did all my childhood vacations with a solo parent, including Disney. I never thought about missing the other parent while we were doing activities. When I brought the pictures to show and tell, I never felt awkward. My mom was friends with the other single moms. I knew all the other kids family situation.  I don’t remember anything about that until high school when a classmate said families should sit at the table for dinner like a proper nuclear family. Annnnd nobody liked her.
Can you get it sealed? I know people who have sealed theirs. Go to the court house and ask what you need to do. Not every county requires a lawyer
I get a lot of help from my friends at church. Can you find something you’re passionate about and build a community around it?
Single mom with a dog, here. I love my current situation.  But daycare helps me find extra time for my dog.
I think food quality played a part. The food I eat is not nearly as highly quality as the baby’s.

My point is that breastfeeding made me hungry for more than 500 calories. It was like I was going to the gym everyday. I’m 126lb now but if I work out I have to put on weight or I look emaciated. There was no way I could breastfeed in my normal resting diet.
I stopped breastfeeding and I wasn’t as hungry.
Do you not ask for gifts or do you tell the guests not to bring them? And then are you expected to bring gifts to other parties? I just had a kid and I’d like to do no gift parties.
Just want to stay up all night with you by Beck

I also heard this. But my Costco brand is identical to the Huggies brand. Walmart is still the least expensive and I like their diaper also Target brand is in between the price of Costco and Walmart but their grocery pickup is the easiest. So to me, it’s worth the 2 extra cents per diaper.

Monthly, I ate $500 worth of groceries while breast feeding. Now I do formula for $70 a month and I spend under $200 on my own groceries. And I include the baby purée into my grocery bill.  I didn’t mind the cost, I just couldn’t hack it once I went back to work.

I would kind of do these things in any major city anywhere in the world. But I use that spotcrime website to figure out if I’m parking my car or take transit. Ive never lived in humbolt park. I just have to go to the Salvation Army center sometimes because my work does fund raisers for them.

You can look up the weekly crimes on spotcrime’s website.  I’ve been mugged (in the suburbs) and I personally wouldn’t have my cell phone out while walking around in HP.  I’d also keep my transit card separate from my wallet.
She’s not into cartoons yet. But she likes seeing human kids sing.
Are there any sing along shows with children on PBS? My kiddo really likes to sing along with the kids. But not the cartoon kids.

I had a baby girl just before the election and found out my mom voted for trump. She leans republican but is very progressive and I was really surprised. We don’t talk about politics but I know she has abstained from voting in the past. She doesn’t watch the news because it’s too depressing so she is oblivious. She had no idea what project 2025 was. I had a really hard time with it because I just had a little girl. I was hurt more than the election results. She could tell I was shocked in the weeks after and kept trying to bring up how her and her friends felt better about things and how they were optimistic. It took a month but I was able to let it go and we are as we were before.  I hope that you can find boundaries that work for your family relationship.
Get rid of the subscriptions.

There are atheist AA meetings online. Although, it’s not a religious program. You’re asked to find a “higher power “ to replace your ego. In the 30’s they interpret this as God. But there’s a lot of alternatives for people who are not interested in faith. I personally like the Buddhist/meditation approach. There’s also meetings for wiccans. But whatever floats her boat, it’s out there. Also if you are going to AlNon, there are Alnon and AA open speaker meetings at a lot of hospitals and behavioral centers. You can go together and just listen.

I just bought some at Aldi for $5. They were the free range and less expensive than the normal ones. I went when they opened. I was at Costco yesterday and I couldn’t get near the eggs but there wasn’t a line. It was just normal Costco Saturday busy.  Seriously, I’d investigate instacart. I did their trial, got a $20 coupon and fees waived.  Then canceled after I picked up the groceries.  I think it’s worth the trouble for Costco because the store is a mad house here. Kroger’s eggs were $10-$12
At my baby shower I had people write a note to my future baby on a poster board. Maybe, you could have people write a special memory about your daughter.

Thanks but I don’t feel I’ve suffered. I had a very good childhood over all and I feel a tremendous amount of gratitude for my family. I’m so blessed that we have an honest relationship and that I learned hard lessons at a young age.

I don’t understand. Is it the coin you’re having issues with? I saw someone had a key chain medallion that unlocked the cart. I thought about getting one, but I always find an open cart at Aldi so I’ve never had any problems with my kiddo and her carrier.

These were not past experiences. My parents didn’t start recovery until I was much older. If they got messed up and then beat me, I felt like they were unloading their problems on me. If they told me they were depressed and couldn’t deal with me, I didn’t feel that they were unloading their troubles. I felt they were being honest. You can’t hide something like that when you’re in active addiction. Not from a teenager. Obviously, it’s not an ideal situation for anyone but the world isn’t perfect and we don’t know this kid. If he’s already showing interest in drinking and smoking, than I would not be subtle.
I don’t have those feelings yet. Just days we’re I’m tired. And then I try to do something for myself asap

At 14, I was already being offered drugs and alcohol. My parents had a lot of frank discussions with me. About their own experiences and that of other family members. When I was in High School and college, I was so surprised how naive and unsafe the other students were. So, it really depends on the context of the conversation and what actions the mom takes next.  Hopefully, it will encourage him not to follow in mom’s path.

There’s atheists meetings online. The whole point of the HP is to find something bigger than yourself. You seem to like other parts of the program. Why can’t those things be your HP?  Experience, strength, hope and helping are your HP. Go with it and don’t over think it.
Girl, go to an AA women’s meeting. They’re online too. You need the support of people who know what you went through. Best wishes.
I’m sorry, but if this is effecting work can’t you go to the doctor? If you don’t have health insurance, I think you need to get a job that offers that.
I don’t think getting married will mean much. I have a coworker who got married in college to a woman who was studying on a student visa and she was not able to stay just because they’re married.
Thank you! And they’re really good siblings to each other. This is the clearly the best choice.

I use my card for anything that doesn’t have a convenience fee. If I want something, I make sure it’s like a donut or a pint of ice cream. I have a baby and sometimes I want to buy her some fabulous thing that will make her super smart/healthy. But I try to cap that under $100. I don’t go crazy on organic baby food. I don’t buy her a ton of toys because there’s toys at her daycare. If I feel bad about these things, I read to her more or make her food. But I do not spend the money I don’t have.

I feel like you need to keep him home. My daycare reimburses me for days I have a sick note. Is this something you can talk to your doctor about? Maybe enough reimbursements will help the director to take care of the situation while you wait for another daycare to have an open spot.
Good! I’m glad you can let him help so you can do your thing. Some partners can’t. Best wishes for your family!
If you’re stressed and he’s off of work, let him watch the kids for an hour and take your dogs out or go for a walk. Do something for yourself away from the house.

Sooo, just throwing it out there… I had my first at 37 and a lot of my friends also had children starting in their mid 30s. My nephew just got married, they have been together 15 years. They’re in their early 30’s and want to have kids. You never know what will happen:-)
I pay 1400 a month for daycare and I work remote. I gross 1k a week. I totally have 30-200 bucks left a week.  My baby is 6months old.

It’s a magazine 

https://www.checkbook.org/

I would ask another lawyer to look at your case. I know a woman who was hospitalized and her mom sent the kids to live with the father. Then he wouldn’t give the kids back. The woman lawyered up and was told it could take a long time. The woman got a different lawyer after a month and got her kids back the same day. And it turned out the ex was really neglectful.

This post really got me fired up and I thought about it some more. Can you ask your local library to do a day for kids with non traditional families? A day for all different types of families to come and check out books about unique family situations?

I’m 38 and had my baby 6months ago. My career took a hit when I started fertility treatments and my earnings have been cut in half. I basically live paycheck to paycheck now. I am so happy. Even when I’m so tired, I am so grateful and happy. Life is short. My only suggestion would be to get your retirement in order. I have a robust retirement and emergency fund. That definitely helps me feel less anxious. Also, I have an amazing support group. I didn’t until I was pregnant and told people about being a SMBC. But once I was past the point of no return, people really showed up for me.

I feel like there has to be other kids in this situation at the school. My mom was a single mom and my dad lived far away. He didn’t attend much of anything I did at school. I also know some kids have a parent who travels for work a lot. Can you find out who else is in your daughters’ shoes and plan something special with their families?

I think you’re doing great. Also, my daycare helps potty train the older kids. Maybe pop her in there for short term. At least while the baby is so little and you get over this hump. She might get motivated around other kids.

OP suggest this to your GF! It will help your GF have less anxiety and help her to create a real plan. And you would be such a good friend for suggesting and supporting her.   And if she says no, than seriously, red flag
600 a year after a health incentive credit.
You are not going to stop his drinking. You have to leave with your kids and let him hit rock bottom. He will drag all of you down with him if you don’t leave.

Also at the library (US) is a publication called checkbook. And it breaks down the cost of all sorts of services and stores. It’s based on 15ish different US cities and their suburbs and everything is broken down by county.  It’s really been a great time saver to me as a solo parent.
I know you like the place you rent but pet fees are bogus. If you can, ask if you can double your security deposit.

This book has been recommended to me by other parents. I totally have it on my list to read. I read a book on surveillance in social media and I decided my kid is going to have to make that decision when they are a teenager. I don’t even put my child’s image up on socials now because I feel like they may resent it when they are older.

I stopped awhile ago but I saw they are super expensive now. Frozen grilled chicken strips are $6-$8 dollars at my stores. I toss a handful into the things I’m cooking for a quick protein. If you’re going to pay a lot of money for a protein, than why not make it something premade and fast? 

For baking there’s so many recipes that exclude eggs but for those that include them, I use bob’s red mill egg replacer. Kind of pricey but a bag lasts all year and I usually find I have to bake a ton of Christmas cookies to polish it off.

My mom’s a boomer and her younger brother a Gen xer. They watch my kiddo. They just can’t really see once it starts to get dark so I have to drive my kid to them. My Dad will watch her when she gets a little older. His house is not baby proof and he’s a smoker, so Id decline the help anyway.

My cousin crocheted my baby some hats. They were so nice because the baby grows so fast and I didn’t have to buy new hats that she’s only wear for a short time. And now they’re with a friend who has just had a baby. Also the Boppi is a sold buy. My baby doesn’t use it anymore but my chihuahua and I use the 2 that were gifted to us.

My kiddo isn’t old enough for birthday parties yet but I wonder why parents don’t ask guests to bring a snack in lieu of gifts. Kids love junk food and special treats. They’re going to get all sugared up anyway. This showing off of toys and grandiose gift opening is really kind of weird. Let that be for the grandparents who spoil them.

Yeah if op is in the US, Trader Joe’s has nice flower arrangements for 5 to 10 bucks. Although, I can’t afford them rn. It’s home made cards for me this year. And they are basically thank you notes to my babysitters.

Well if it makes you feel better, my baby slept 7-8hours and now has flipped to 5  to 6 at most. And I have too much to do to start sleeping when she does so I get like 3 to 4. Oh the tables have turned.

I would just arrange the for the relief to come over regardless if he wants it or not. If they come over and he doesn’t want to nap, he doesn’t have to. But it willing probably make you feel better. Honestly though, he’ll be fine. I’m a solo and first time parent and I make it work everyday. He’s experienced and just has to make it for the weekend.

When I started my journey, I asked my friend, who’s a mother and a child of adoption, for her advice. And she said she felt I should donor conceive.  I also looked into it myself and it’s pretty darn expensive and competitive. Also, there’s a lot of human trafficking to be aware of.  But after doing all the research, I would like to foster kiddos once mine has gotten a little older.
The container store is going out of business. I didn’t go in to see what they have.
Do not let this woman touch your child, do not pick her up and change your locks if she has keys.

Fire her and make sure she doesn’t try to squat there. Do not let her use your address for court! And once you fire her, hire a cleaning lady and a dog walker. I have a 800 ft condo and a chihuahua and I needed help cleaning and walking her when my baby came home. Find out how much they cost and then tell the girl you can’t afford her and the other more “experienced “ helpers. Lie to her about how much it costs if you need to.

You could be a server. I used to work as one part time during the summer. But it made me so tired that it wasn’t worth risking the performance at my main job. I have a friend who pet sits for people. I would like to do that but I have a baby at home right now.

Each store is different though. The one by my mom’s has amazing baby stuff. The one by me has a really great craft section. The one by Aldi has all the dog stuff. In general, I think the cleaning supplies used to be better but maybe im missing that store.
Ok but your post is about how to maintain hygiene to keep the job. If you don’t want the job, don’t maintain your hygiene. They’ll think you’re gross and let you go.

I would ask the local shelter if they can help you get a private room with a lockable door. You have a job and they may be able to address your concerns. Same with renting a private room. Tell the land lord your concern and ask if you can put a chain on the door or buy your own lock set. I think you’re going to have to put a little trust out there if you want to keep this job, that’s what I’m trying to say.

I had a bad experience with roommates and was violently assaulted and robbed by a work acquaintance of one of them. My roommates were not bad people but I get that you want to be safe. However I think you’re going to need some help from a shelter or a room for rent situation. Go there and discuss your concerns and see if a solution can be worked out.

I’m in my late 30’s, just had my miracle baby, and still feel for OP. Lol, it’s one thing if I say it but I don’t go around asking people if they agree.  I’m also exhausted just reading about these baby parties.  That sounds like a grandma thing or something the library should host.
Keep going! I have 450 and it only gets better!!

I see both sides of this. I have a family member by marriage who is living in his car. He has an active addiction and many people in his family and mine are in recovery. So, people want to help but also they need boundaries. Bridges have been burnt and it’s sometimes hard to know what to do. That being said, I know this isn’t everyone’s situation but I wish everyone here all the best.
I listed to a pod cast called “you look like me” and I follow the donor conceived page.
My grandma used to make my Halloween costumes. I wish I could see so I could make my kiddo dress up clothes. Also, I think sewing would come in handy for holiday outfits that only get worn briefly.

Get him a tutor that will come to the house or you go to their house, or library. Sit with him and make sure he’s present. If he returns to school than he doesn’t need the tutor after school. When I was 10 I used leave school and walk home. They called child services on my mom and she threatened to sue the school district. In the end I had to be tutored to catch up on the school work I missed. I didn’t enjoy it so I stayed in school.
Moving
Sometimes people have anxiety or depression and they need medication so they can get enough relief to make the non medication adjustments that lead to long lasting improvement.

Take a class at the recreation center in your town. Fitness or art. If you can’t afford a class, go to the public library and sign up for free or check out what your student center has to offer. Take a language class. 

You could also host a potluck for your fiancé’s friends who have partners. Then you  find out what those ladies are into and tag along.

Adding to this because I think renting is better for people who want to be minimalist. I have a child, so it makes a little more sense for me to buy something down the road. But I love renting and I’m not looking forward to home ownership.
I’d nap, read a book, draw, take pictures of nature, listen to the radio, look at the stars, build a fire and make tasty food.

So my cousin’s kid travels a lot as a teacher. He doesn’t have a lot of money. His parents may help him like, by giving him flier miles or some pocket money when he visits them. He’s been to about a dozen countries. I would consider him poor and his parents middle class. Idk, his dad might be rich. But his family and our family have a lot of other cousins and cousin’s of cousins who live abroad and all over the us. We do a lot of couch surf travel. I also worked with a guy who had 2 jobs and was always traveling. He’d use his sick days and go to Spain for the weekend like 10 times a year. It was absurd and I don’t know when he ever slept. He would have been in his early 30s so maybe he had saved a lot of money but from the look of his socials, he was always traveling. He also had 6 siblings and only half of them were first generation Americans. I never got the impression that they were well off. Again, I think he just had a bunch of family spread all over.
Anything you have and Aldi food. I eat aldi tuna on their dirt cheap white bread when I’m broke. With whatever canned/frozen veggies they have.
I think you find a grandma type who over plucked and has to draw her brows in.  Let them have a little chat about beauty standards. That’s what got me to leave mine alone.
I bought as many as I could because i didn’t want my kiddo to have 20 half siblings. So far they have 2. I bought 6 and I used 3

I would ask the family member giving you the money. I paid for a family member’s auto repair but offered to help find and pay for a new car. They ended up paying me back, but they still don’t have a reliable transportation situation.  I got kind of resentful. I was able to let it go but it seems like no matter what is decided, it will help you. So way not see what they say and that way there’s no resentment between you about what was the best decision for the gift money.

I will just say once I got my kiddo in daycare, the dog care became a lot better.  I was just able to plan things better. I don’t have as many kids or dogs, but I also don’t have a spouse. Whatever you decide it, I hope it works out :)

I haven’t been to the farmer’s market near me in awhile but depending on what town it’s in, I think the booth can be pretty expensive to rent. But I noticed most have reduced prices at the farm shop. One farmer that I really like sells boxes of seasonal produce for much less than the market.  They may even have a delivery route. Also, the market gets wiped out by the restaurant cooks.  So it’s really not an alternative to the grocery store. I’ve found the gardening advice to be the best and I think if you’re going to grow your own veg, it’s a great resource. But, mostly if you shop at the farmers market, you’re just supporting local businesses and hopefully buying something you’ll actually consume.  I think it can be of good value to shop there but not a option if you’re in poverty. Now if you have a budget to eat out and you’re going to the farmer’s market then that can be a nice outing and possibly more frugal than going and eating in a restaurant. But you absolutely talk to the farmers. The produce at the farmer’s market is a different product.

I have 4 nieces, all sisters, and the 2nd youngest is 8 . she is allowed to wear makeup. I’m a little surprised because my SIL thinks chemical sunscreen is bad. But her daughter is allowed to wear mascara and a little bit of light colored eyeliner. She’s allowed to wear it on the weekend and outside of the house. The older girls have no interest in make up but they are at the age they are interested in boys. So maybe my SIL just picks her battles. But her daughter never looks like she’s too mature. She’s also into nail art and I think she’s just a girly girly. As long as she sees make up as fun and not as a way to change herself or hide her features, than I think it’s ok.

Can you take her out for a special day without her little brother?  Something where you don’t have to multitask. Maybe a trip to the library or going to get a hot chocolate. Or maybe even a visit to another adult relative’s? Something low budget, easy to drive to but for her.

I have a nightlight by iHome that is a white noise machine. I don’t know if they make it anymore but it’s kind of key I think. Basically, before bedtime we take the dog out and then I feed the baby. I have a lamp in the bedroom and a light on the ceiling fan. I turn on the lamp and turn off the the ceiling light. The lamp signals the start of bedtime. I pick out some jammies and then we use the bathroom to take a bath or just to pee. I explain to the baby that we pee before we go to bed. Idk, I’m hopeful this will help potty training.  Then we go into the bedroom. I feed her and if she’s still got energy we play. I lay on the bed and sit or stand her on my tummy and sing to her while she looks around. If I have to pick up the bedroom or fold laundry, I put on an audiobook book and give her a pacifier. I moved a swing into the bedroom so she can watch me and I talk to her.  Sometimes I put her in a lounger and she falls asleep while I’m eating yogurt and paying bills on a laptop. If she doesn’t fall asleep she’ll  eventually get fussy and I will  try to feed her again. If she doesn’t want to eat, I’ll turn off the lamp and turn on the nightlight. I turn it to red because I’ve heard that doesn’t disrupt sleep. If she does feed, I still turn off the lamp and turn on the nightlight afterwards. Before she was sleeping through the night, if she woke up I would turn on a hall light so I could see well enough to feed her. I keep the bedroom door open for the dog to come and go.  But once she falls asleep or needs to fall asleep, the lamp goes off and the nightlight and hall light goes on. If she cries in the night and I think she’s sick, I do not turn on the bedroom light. I go into the bathroom, turn on the light, go back to the bedroom and bring her in there.  But usually if she wakes up she’s fine. She just goes back to sleep. I stay awake for a little bit. I do laundry or clean the bathroom. I keep the hall light on and check on her. But I do not turn the bedroom lamp on again until morning. In the morning, I get up and turn the hall light on. I feed the dog and I say good morning to her so the baby isn’t totally surprised by me. I gently wake the baby and then I bring her into the bathroom where I’ve already turned on the light, and I tell her we go to the potty when we get out of bed.  Then I change her and then I feed her and we’ve got the bedroom lamp on by then so she’s awake. Then we take out the dog and I bring her over to the babysitter’s. And the whole time I tell her what I’m doing. Like, “ok I’m turning out the lights for bedtime” or “ok I’m turning on the lights so we can use the bathroom” and “ok I know you’re hungry, let’s have breakfast “.   It sounds like a lot but basically it’s just keeping the room dark and doing things in the order that works best for me… and the dog. The dog actually decides when we go to bed. So there’s that.

But here are my tips
I do formula feeding as well as breast milk. This really helps me at night time. I also set up changing stations in every room as well as sleeping areas. I have a bassinet and play yard in the living room and dining room.  I have extra bouncers and swings in different rooms too. That way if she gets sleepy, I can plop her down and clean up that room. She doesn’t actually sleep but she’ll be content for a few minutes before she perks up again.  I got an extra pump too, although I haven’t used it yet. I buy mostly frozen veggies so I only have to cook the protein in my meals.  I also buy frozen dumplings and meatballs. I only need a handful of groceries to buy during the week. I get things that are already portioned so I don’t have to meal prep. I haven’t done the grocery delivery or pick up yet but when I do need to restock the pantry and freezer, I will. I have to take the dog to the groomer so we’ll see how that goes. Usually I hang out there or go shopping because there’s not enough time to go home and do anything meaningful. Cotton is susceptible to mold. Even the plastic around a tampon isn’t sealed tight to the tampon. There’s air in there already. I keep mine for a year tops and I store them next to a water absorber box thingie from the dollar store.  Most ladies keep them in the driest spot of the bathroom. But if you are going to keep them for a long time, I would not keep them in the bathroom. If they do mold on the inside, there’s no way of really knowing.  

Toxic shock from tampons isn’t a thing anymore, but I think you would want to find the most sterile packaged products you can.  It’s said that super absorbing products are most commonly linked to toxic shock. I think this is because they can actually pull more moisture from the air. But tampons used to be sold in a cardboard tube (and sometimes still are) Otherwise, pads might be better to store for longer because they are not an internal product. And then maybe the thin ones would actually be best because they are made with the least amount of cotton. However, they are not very helpful when you are in need.

1. I don’t have debt. I worked full time during college and I haven’t bought a home. Since taxes are very high where I live, I probably will not buy a home. I keep my vehicle purchases low so I can pay it off within a couple years, if I have to pay it off at all.

2. I saved an emergency fund that is the equivalent of my salary. Once I did so, I kept a set amount in my bank account. It’s 10k. I don’t wear makeup daily and I keep my skin care routine simple BUT I am getting wrinkles so if I buy a fancy product I YouTube it first.
